newsitem.title: CHINA: Southern Airlines mulls A-share offering in China.
newsitem.headline: Southern Airlines mulls A-share offering in China.

text.p: China Southern Airlines Co Ltd intends to offer up to 500 million A-shares to Chinese investors subject to approval by relevant authorities, the airline operator said in its listing propectus obtained on Monday.
China Southern Airlines said the proposed A share offering would not be made earlier than 180 days from the date of the prospectus.
The offering price per share of the A shares will not be less than the Renminbi equivalent of the issue price of the H-shares in the Hong Kong offering.
"There can be no assurance as to whether or when the proposed A share offering will be completed," it said.
It gave no further details on the A-shares offering.
A-shares are Chinese enterprises shares listed in Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges earmarking for domestic investors only. H-shares are enterprises shares listed in Hong Kong.

The Guangzhou based airline operator had said on Monday it was issuing 1.03 billion H-shares in global flotation of which 71 million H-shares are being offered in Hong Kong at a price ranging from HK$3.71 to HK$4.70 each.
It said the shares would be priced as close of the Hong Kong public offer on July 25. Dealing in the company's H-shares in Hong Kong is expected to commence on July 31.
Goldman Sachs (Asia) L.L.C. is the global coordinator, sponsor and manager of the issue.

Among the total, 71 million H-shares are offered to the public in Hong Kong, 353.51 million will be sold under the U.S. offering in the form of American Depository Shares, 573.29 million shares for international placement in the form of ADS and to strategic investors. The remaining 32.2 million new H-shares are placed with Goldman Sachs and Co.

China Southern Airlines said it the prospectus that it would continue to expand and rationalise its operation so as to increase profitability of its route network, with 270 routes serving 68 destinations.
It said it would also integrate flight training, aircraft maintenance and air catering operations, and would continue to invest in aviation infrastructure including information systems.
